summary: Destructor-style teardown for a small object owning a double pointer. Reads the flag byte at this+8; when it is set and the owning pointer at this+0 is non-null, the inner allocation (*v2) is freed first via FreeWrapper_7bcf, then the outer pointer v2 itself is freed. Returns the flag value read at entry; when the flag is clear the object is left untouched.

local_names.this: object holding an ownership flag (this+8) and an owned double pointer (this+0)
local_names.v2: outer pointer (LPVOID*) loaded from this+0; *v2 is the inner allocation
local_names.result: flag byte read from this+8, also the function return value

operations.description: Reads the flag byte at this+8; if it is zero the function returns immediately without freeing anything.
When the flag is set, loads the owning pointer from this+0 and proceeds only if it is non-null.
If the inner allocation (*v2, first pointer of the object at this+0) is non-null, it is freed first with FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Frees the outer pointer v2 with FreeWrapper_7bcf and returns the saved flag value.
Invoked by sub_431BE0, DirectoryFileEnumerator (00431DB0) and StandingsDisplay (0046A560) as a teardown helper.

unresolved: Whether the byte at this+8 is a reference count or an ownership flag, and what the inner/outer allocations own, is unknown
